flashcards.question: How is the first midterm structured?
flashcards.answer: 10 questions total: 5 closed-type + 5 open-type short answers.
flashcards.explanation: The test focuses on Tourism Geography of Croatia and core geography basics.

flashcards.question: How many points does the blind map carry?
flashcards.answer: 10 points total.
flashcards.explanation: Each correctly located toponym on the map is worth 1 point.

flashcards.question: Which categories are used on the blind map?
flashcards.answer: 2 county centres, 2 bigger islands, 1 national park, 1 nature park, 4 top tourist destinations.
flashcards.explanation: These categories are explicitly listed in the 1st midterm instructions.

flashcards.question: What is the total exam duration for 1st midterm + blind map?
flashcards.answer: 20 minutes total (15 + 5).
flashcards.explanation: Timing discipline matters because map part is short and fast-paced.

flashcards.question: What should students not ignore while studying slides?
flashcards.answer: Photos, graphics, and statistics.
flashcards.explanation: Instructions explicitly mention image-based and visual recognition tasks.

learn.title: How to Prepare for the 1st Midterm (Exact Format)
learn.content:
Official Structure

  • Written test: 10 questions (5 closed + 5 open)
  • Blind map: 10 terms to locate in Croatia
  • Total duration: 20 minutes (15 + 5)

Blind Map Categories

2 county centres + 2 bigger islands + 1 national park + 1 nature park + 4 top destinations

Mandatory Map Focus

Use both maps in Learn mode: county-centre orientation and protected-areas orientation.

Practical Rule

Toponym must be connected to the right location (dot/circle/marker). Name without location is not accepted.

High-Score Strategy

Train map placement with county map and protected-area map, then drill Top 10 destinations as a separate set.

flashcards.question: What is the origin and meaning of the word "geography"?
flashcards.answer: From Ancient Greek γεωγραφία (geōgraphía) = "earth description". Geography studies Earth's features and the relationships between people and their environments.
flashcards.explanation: The object of study of geography is the space that surrounds us.

flashcards.question: What approach does the course use to reach Tourism Geography?
flashcards.answer: A deductive approach — it starts with a general overview of Geography and gradually narrows the focus until reaching Tourism Geography.
flashcards.explanation: General geography → regional geography → tourism geography.

flashcards.question: What is Regional Geography about?
flashcards.answer: Combining knowledge from different disciplines to understand regions, and understanding the relationships and processes in real geographical space to make projections for future development.
flashcards.explanation: This reflects the interdisciplinary nature of geography.

flashcards.question: What are the three main fields of interest of Human Geography?
flashcards.answer: Population, Economy, and Settlements.
flashcards.explanation: Population (distribution, migrations, diversity, globalization); Economy (resources, economic activity, core–periphery, four economic sectors); Settlements (patterns, physical structures, cultural diversity, urbanization).

flashcards.question: What does Tourism Geography study?
flashcards.answer: Tourism resources and attractions, specific tourism locations/areas/regions, and regional characteristics and differences.
flashcards.explanation: It examines the spatial (geographical) factors influencing tourism — environment, society, and economy.

flashcards.question: Why is Tourism Geography considered interdisciplinary?
flashcards.answer: Because, like other geography disciplines, it incorporates elements of both physical geography and human geography.
flashcards.explanation: It combines natural and social factors that shape tourism and the space around us.

flashcards.question: How is a "tourist destination" defined?
flashcards.answer: A geographical area whose total tourist product (brand) — the result of natural and/or social tourist factors and attractions — is recognizable on the tourist market.
flashcards.explanation: Branding and market recognizability are what make an area a destination.

flashcards.question: By which three criteria are regions singled out in geography?
flashcards.answer: (1) natural characteristics (physical geography); (2) human-made characteristics (human geography); (3) the interaction of human and natural environment.
flashcards.explanation: This is the basis of regionalization.

flashcards.question: Why are Geography and Tourism Geography important?
flashcards.answer: For understanding spatial patterns and for decision-making and planning.
flashcards.explanation: Recognizing patterns on the map supports better development decisions.

flashcards.question: What are the "four economic sectors" referred to in human geography?
flashcards.answer: Primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary.
flashcards.explanation: The Economy field covers resources, economic activity/factors, core–periphery structure, and the four sectors.

learn.title: Introduction to Geography & Tourism Geography
learn.content:
What Is Geography?

The word comes from Ancient Greek γεωγραφία (geōgraphía) — literally "earth description". Geography studies Earth's features and the relationships between people and their environments. Its object of study is the space that surrounds us.

Deductive path of the course: general Geography → Regional Geography → Tourism Geography

An Interdisciplinary Science

Geography combines knowledge from disciplines with different objects of research. Regional geography uses this to understand regions and the processes in real geographical space, so we can make projections for future development.

Human Geography — Three Fields of Interest

  • Population: distribution, migrations, diversity, globalization
  • Economy: resources, economic activity & factors, core–periphery structure, the four economic sectors (primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary)
  • Settlements: settlement patterns, physical structures, cultural diversity, urbanization

What Tourism Geography Studies

  • Tourism resources analysis and tourism attractions
  • Specific tourism locations, areas, or regions
  • Regional characteristics and differences
  • The spatial factors influencing tourism — shaping environment, society, and economy

Tourist Destination

A geographical area whose total tourist product (brand) — the result of natural and/or social tourist factors and attractions — is recognizable on the tourist market.

Regionalization — Regions Are Singled Out By

  1. Natural characteristics (physical geography)
  2. Human-made characteristics (human geography)
  3. The interaction of the human and natural environment

Why It Matters

Geography helps us understand spatial patterns and supports decision-making and planning — the foundation for everything that follows about Croatia.

learn.title: Blind Map Categories and Location Logic
learn.content:
What You Actually Place on the Map

  • 2 county centres
  • 2 bigger islands
  • 1 national park
  • 1 nature park
  • 4 top destinations (from Top 10 table)

How to Drill Efficiently

  1. Start with county centres and coast orientation
  2. Add islands by north-to-south chain
  3. Place NP and PP by region anchors
  4. Finish with Top 10 destination set

Common Error

Students know names but miss exact placement. Practice spatial memory, not just memorization.

flashcards.question: What mountain system shapes Croatian relief, and how was it formed?
flashcards.answer: The Dinarides — part of the Alpide belt — formed by tectonic plates colliding during the Alpine orogeny, which began in the Cretaceous period.
flashcards.explanation: Relief examples from the slides: Žumberak, Velebit, Kornati, Baranja, Lonjsko polje.

flashcards.question: What are the three karst surface forms, with their slide examples?
flashcards.answer: Covered karst (beech & fir forests of the Croatian Highlands, e.g. Plitvice), Semi-covered karst (maquis, e.g. Cres), and Bare karst (no vegetation, e.g. island Pag).
flashcards.explanation: Karst (limestone) dominates the Croatian landscape; see also Velebit karst doline and Biokovo.

flashcards.question: What are maquis (makija)?
flashcards.answer: Degraded Mediterranean coastal forest whose typical representative is the holm oak; the example of semi-covered karst vegetation (e.g. Cres).
flashcards.explanation: Maquis marks the transition between bare and forested karst.

flashcards.question: What are the key characteristics of the Adriatic Sea in Croatian hydrography?
flashcards.answer: Salinity ~38‰, warm currents, turquoise colour, excellent transparency, and low tide amplitudes.
flashcards.explanation: These features directly underpin Croatia's bathing/sea-tourism image.

flashcards.question: Describe Croatia's inland waters from the slides.
flashcards.answer: Clear karst rivers in the mountain area, travertine barriers, a small number of lakes, and larger Pannonian rivers with poor navigability — except the Danube.
flashcards.explanation: Examples: Mrežnica, Drava–Mura, Plitvice lakes; Kopački rit on the Danube floodplain.

flashcards.question: What climate type does Croatia have?
flashcards.answer: A temperate climate (type C): Mediterranean along the coast and continental inland.
flashcards.explanation: Slides note Adriatic winds, sea temperature (winter/summer), insolation, and rainfall.

flashcards.question: What are the four biogeographic regions of Croatia?
flashcards.answer: Alpine, Continental, Mediterranean, and Pannonian.
flashcards.explanation: Shown together with protected areas (e.g. NP Risnjak in the Alpine bioregion).

flashcards.question: What was Croatia's GDP per capita in 2025 (Croatia ID card slide)?
flashcards.answer: About 23,200 EUR — roughly 80% of the EU GDP per capita.
flashcards.explanation: The tourism share of Croatia's GDP is about 20 to 25%.

flashcards.question: What were the ten Pan-European transport corridors, and when were they defined?
flashcards.answer: Strategic transport routes in Central and Eastern Europe, defined at the Helsinki conference in 1997.
flashcards.explanation: Context for Croatia's connectivity (cultural regions of Europe and Croatia).

flashcards.question: Name the key transport infrastructure shown for Croatia.
flashcards.answer: Highways A1–A12, the Učka tunnel, Krk bridge, Pelješac bridge, and the Drava bridge; main airports Zagreb and Split; sea/inland traffic via coastal shipping, cruises, charter and private boats.
flashcards.explanation: Lecture 3 covers road, air, and sea/inland water traffic.

flashcards.question: Which demographic processes affect Croatia (and its tourism)?
flashcards.answer: Population aging, low birth rate, immigration, emigration, deruralization, urbanization/suburbanization, and population substitution.
flashcards.explanation: Consequences on tourism: labour-market changes (shortage, selective economic immigration) and changing emission-market characteristics.

flashcards.question: What are the features of Croatia's population density?
flashcards.answer: Uneven density, dominance of the capital (Zagreb), four-to-five regional centres, littoralization, deruralization, and depopulation.
flashcards.explanation: Littoralization = population concentrating along the coast.

flashcards.question: How many residence & work permits were issued in 2025, and to which sectors?
flashcards.answer: 170,723 permits total: Construction 31%, Tourism & hospitality 31%, Industries 14%, Transport & communication 8%, Trade 5%, Other 11%.
flashcards.explanation: Tourism and construction together absorb the majority of foreign labour.

flashcards.question: Which countries received the most Croatian work permits in 2025?
flashcards.answer: Bosnia and Herzegovina (32,225), Nepal (31,708), Serbia (24,278), Philippines (17,629), and India (15,400).
flashcards.explanation: Immigrants are mostly seasonal auxiliary workforce in tourism, with a rising trend toward permanent residence.

flashcards.question: How does the changing labour force affect tourist destinations?
flashcards.answer: It changes the autochthonousness of destinations — language, culture, behaviour, gastronomy, and the perception of security.
flashcards.explanation: A key social consequence of economic immigration.

flashcards.question: How are Croatia's tourism numbers characterized in the slides?
flashcards.answer: A return to pre-pandemic growth, dominated by international tourism (traditional Central-European emitive markets) and a distinct summer (bathing) seasonality.
flashcards.explanation: Foreign tourists clearly dominate over domestic ones.

learn.title: Core Features of Croatia for the Midterm
learn.content:
Physical / Natural Features (Lecture 2)

  • Relief: the Dinarides (Alpide belt), formed by colliding tectonic plates in the Alpine orogeny (from the Cretaceous). Examples: Žumberak, Velebit, Kornati, Baranja, Lonjsko polje.
  • Karst: Covered (beech/fir forests of the Highlands, e.g. Plitvice) · Semi-covered (maquis / holm oak, e.g. Cres) · Bare (no vegetation, e.g. Pag).
  • Climate: temperate (type C) — Mediterranean coast, continental inland; key factors: Adriatic winds, sea temperature, insolation, rainfall.
  • Hydrography: Adriatic — 38‰ salinity, warm currents, turquoise colour, excellent transparency, low tides. Inland — clear karst rivers, travertine barriers, few lakes, poorly navigable Pannonian rivers except the Danube (Mrežnica, Drava–Mura).
  • Biogeographic regions: Alpine, Continental, Mediterranean, Pannonian.

Human / Social Features (Lecture 3)

  • Economy (2025): GDP/cap ~23,200 EUR (≈80% of EU average); tourism = 20–25% of GDP.
  • Transport: highways A1–A12, Učka tunnel, Krk bridge, Pelješac bridge, Drava bridge; main airports Zagreb & Split; sea/inland traffic (coastal shipping, cruises, charter, private boats). Pan-European corridors defined at Helsinki 1997.
  • Population: uneven density, capital dominance (Zagreb), 4–5 regional centres, littoralization, deruralization, depopulation. Processes: aging, low birth rate, migration, urbanization, population substitution.
  • Tourism numbers: return to pre-pandemic growth, international tourism dominant, distinct summer seasonality.

Work & Residence Permits 2025 (170,723 total)

By sector: Construction 31% · Tourism & hospitality 31% · Industries 14% · Transport & communication 8% · Trade 5% · Other 11%.

By country: Bosnia & Herzegovina 32,225 · Nepal 31,708 · Serbia 24,278 · Philippines 17,629 · India 15,400.

Mostly seasonal auxiliary workforce in tourism — changing destinations' language, culture, gastronomy and perception of security.

Exam Tip

Pair each physical feature with a tourism implication: karst → protected areas/diving/scenery; Adriatic transparency → bathing tourism; Dinarides → mountain/adventure tourism.

flashcards.question: What are the three Croatian tourist macro-regions?
flashcards.answer: Coastal, Mountainous, and Pannonian tourist region.
flashcards.explanation: Regional structure appears in multiple lectures.

flashcards.question: Which two strict reserves are listed in slides?
flashcards.answer: Bijele i Samarske stijene; Hajdučki i Rožanski kukovi.

flashcards.question: Name all 8 national parks of Croatia.
flashcards.answer: Plitvička jezera, Krka, Kornati, Brijuni, Mljet, Paklenica, Risnjak, Sjeverni Velebit.
flashcards.explanation: All 8 are shown in lecture 6.

flashcards.question: Name at least 6 nature parks from lecture set.
flashcards.answer: Kopački rit, Medvednica, Papuk, Žumberak, Lonjsko polje, Učka, Telašćica, Velebit, Vransko jezero, Dinara, Biokovo, Lastovsko otočje.
flashcards.explanation: Croatia has 12 nature parks total.

flashcards.question: Which UNESCO site in Croatia is also a national park?
flashcards.answer: Plitvice Lakes.
flashcards.explanation: It appears in both natural protection and UNESCO context.

flashcards.question: What sub-regions make up the North Croatian Coast?
flashcards.answer: Istria and Kvarner.
flashcards.explanation: From lecture 4 on coastal tourist region.

flashcards.question: What sub-regions make up Southern Croatian Coast (Dalmatia)?
flashcards.answer: Northern Dalmatia (Zadar, Šibenik), Central Dalmatia (Trogir, Split, Makarska), South Dalmatia (Dubrovnik).
flashcards.explanation: From lecture 4 detailed coastal breakdown.

flashcards.question: What are the three types of Istria shown in lectures?
flashcards.answer: Red Istria (western/southern coast, red-brown soils), Gray Istria (central, gray clay/flysch), White Istria (Učka/eastern, rocky).
flashcards.explanation: Three-colour model from lecture 4.

flashcards.question: Name key destinations in the Kvarner region from slides.
flashcards.answer: Opatija, Rijeka/Trsat, Crikvenica, Rab, Cres/Lubenice, Lošinj, Punat.
flashcards.explanation: From lecture 4, Kvarner tourist region page.

flashcards.question: Name key Pannonian region destinations from Central Croatia slides.
flashcards.answer: Zagreb, Varaždin, Karlovac, Hrvatsko Zagorje, Trakošćan, Medvednica.
flashcards.explanation: From lecture 5, Pannonian tourist region.

flashcards.question: Name key Pannonian destinations from Eastern Croatia (Slavonija).
flashcards.answer: Osijek, Vukovar, Đakovo, Ilok, Vinkovci, Kopački rit, Papuk.
flashcards.explanation: From lecture 5.

flashcards.question: List all 10 UNESCO tangible heritage sites in Croatia.
flashcards.answer: 1) Diocletian's Palace (Split), 2) Euphrasius Basilica (Poreč), 3) Plitvice Lakes, 4) Trogir, 5) Old City Dubrovnik, 6) Cathedral Šibenik, 7) Stari Grad Plain (Hvar), 8) Medieval tombstones, 9) Venetian Defence (Zadar + St. Nicholas Šibenik), 10) Beech forests (Paklenica, Velebit).
flashcards.explanation: From lecture 6, UNESCO heritage slide.

flashcards.question: How does Croatian law protect nature, and what are the most valuable categories?
flashcards.answer: The Nature Protection Act defines 9 categories of spatial protection; the most valuable are 2 strict reserves, 8 national parks, and 12 nature parks.
flashcards.explanation: National and nature parks together cover 5,930 km² — about 10.1% of Croatia's territory.

flashcards.question: What were the national/nature-park visitor figures for 2017?
flashcards.answer: About 4 million visitors in national and nature parks, of which about 3 million in Plitvice Lakes and Krka; foreign visitors made up 96% of national-park visitors.
flashcards.explanation: Croatia had about 17 million tourists in 2017 (89% foreign, 11% domestic).

flashcards.question: What are the components (types) of natural tourist attractions?
flashcards.answer: Geological, geomorphological, climatological, hydrogeographic, biogeographic, and landscape features.
flashcards.explanation: E.g. caves & canyons (geomorphological), endemics & parks (biogeographic), panoramas (landscape).

flashcards.question: What does the Mountainous tourist region include?
flashcards.answer: Gorski kotar, Risnjak, the Velebit range (northern & southern), Plitvice Lakes and Paklenica; activity spots Platak, Čelimbaša–Mrkopalj, Fužine, Golubinjak, and the Cerovac caves.
flashcards.explanation: From lecture 5 — mountain/adventure and nature tourism.

flashcards.question: What characterizes the Pannonian region — Eastern Croatia (Slavonia)?
flashcards.answer: Osijek, Vukovar (Vučedol, water tower), Ilok and Vinkovci on/near the Danube, Đakovo (Lipizzaner horses), Požega (wine), Papuk (UNESCO Geopark), and Kopački rit.
flashcards.explanation: Etno-cultural heritage events, wine growing, and river/wetland nature.

flashcards.question: What characterizes the Pannonian region — Central Croatia?
flashcards.answer: Zagreb (Advent), Varaždin, Karlovac, Hrvatsko Zagorje (Trakošćan, thermal spas, licitar), Medvednica (Snow Queen skiing), Topusko, and Lonjsko polje (Čigoč stork village).
flashcards.explanation: City-break, spa/wellness, and continental nature tourism.

learn.title: Regional Tourism, Protected Areas, and UNESCO
learn.content:
Tourist Macro-Regions

  • Coastal: Istria (Red/Gray/White), Kvarner (Opatija, Rijeka, islands), Northern Dalmatia (Zadar, Šibenik, Nin), Central Dalmatia (Trogir, Split, Makarska, islands), South Dalmatia (Dubrovnik, Korčula, Ston)
  • Mountainous: Gorski kotar, Velebit range, Plitvice Lakes, Paklenica
  • Pannonian: Central Croatia (Zagreb, Varaždin, Zagorje), Eastern Croatia (Osijek, Vukovar, Đakovo, Baranja)

Protected Areas — Framework & Numbers

The Nature Protection Act defines 9 categories of spatial protection. The most valuable comprise 2 strict reserves + 8 national parks + 12 nature parks. National and nature parks together cover 5,930 km² ≈ 10.1% of Croatia.

Natural attraction components: geological · geomorphological · climatological · hydrogeographic · biogeographic · landscape features.

2017 visitors: ~17 million tourists in Croatia (89% foreign, 11% domestic); ~4 million visited national & nature parks, ~3 million of them in Plitvice Lakes and Krka; foreign visitors were 96% of national-park visitors.

8 National Parks

  1. Plitvička jezera (UNESCO) — covered karst, travertine lakes
  2. Krka — waterfalls, Visovac island monastery
  3. Kornati — 89 islands archipelago
  4. Brijuni — islands near Pula, Roman ruins
  5. Mljet — island park, saltwater lakes
  6. Paklenica — Velebit canyon, climbing (UNESCO beech forests)
  7. Risnjak — Gorski kotar mountain park
  8. Sjeverni Velebit — northern Velebit (UNESCO beech forests)

12 Nature Parks

  1. Kopački rit (Baranja wetland)
  2. Medvednica (mountain above Zagreb)
  3. Papuk (UNESCO Geopark, Slavonia)
  4. Žumberak-Samoborsko gorje
  5. Lonjsko polje (stork village Čigoč)
  6. Učka (above Kvarner coast)
  7. Velebit (broader Velebit range)
  8. Telašćica (Dugi Otok bay)
  9. Vransko jezero (largest natural lake)
  10. Dinara (highest peak 1831m)
  11. Biokovo (above Makarska)
  12. Lastovsko otočje (remote island archipelago)

10 UNESCO Tangible Heritage Sites

  1. Diocletian's Palace — Split
  2. Euphrasius Basilica — Poreč
  3. Plitvice Lakes
  4. Romanesque Town — Trogir
  5. Old City — Dubrovnik
  6. Cathedral of St. James — Šibenik
  7. Stari Grad Plain — Island Hvar
  8. Medieval tombstone graveyards (Stećci)
  9. Venetian Defence System — Zadar walls + St. Nicholas fortress Šibenik
  10. Ancient beech forests — Paklenica + Sjeverni Velebit

Top 10 Tourist Destinations 2024

1. Dubrovnik4,192,151 nights
2. Rovinj4,068,712
3. Poreč3,216,077
4. Split3,070,825
5. Umag2,666,930
6. Zagreb2,646,443
7. Medulin2,615,538
8. Zadar2,299,125
9. Funtana2,098,664
10. Pula2,020,931

Exam Tip

Know the Top 10 by heart — 4 of them appear on your blind map. Also memorize ALL 8 NPs and at least the most important nature parks (Medvednica, Učka, Kopački rit, Biokovo, Papuk, Lonjsko polje).

flashcards.question: What visual cue strongly identifies Dubrovnik?
flashcards.answer: Walled Old Town on a rocky peninsula with distinct fortifications.
flashcards.explanation: This is one of the most recognizable Croatian city panoramas.

flashcards.question: What visual cue strongly identifies Split old core?
flashcards.answer: Dense historic waterfront core linked with Diocletian heritage and ferry-port setting.
flashcards.explanation: Split has a very distinctive urban-maritime skyline.

flashcards.question: What visual cue strongly identifies Makarska?
flashcards.answer: Coastal town directly below steep Biokovo mountain backdrop.
flashcards.explanation: Mountain-wall over coastline is a signature cue.

flashcards.question: What visual cue strongly identifies Ston in this lecture set?
flashcards.answer: Salt pans and defensive walls in a narrow isthmus landscape.
flashcards.explanation: Ston is regularly linked with saltworks and oyster context.

learn.title: How to Solve Image-Based City Questions
learn.content:
Pattern Recognition Method

  1. Identify relief (flat coast vs mountain backdrop)
  2. Identify morphology (walled old town, salt pans, harbor structure)
  3. Connect with regional context from tourist-region slides

High-Confidence Cues

  • Dubrovnik: fortified old city walls
  • Makarska: dramatic Biokovo backdrop
  • Split: major urban waterfront + historic core
  • Ston: salt pans and fortification landscape

flashcards.question: What does the second part of the course (Tourism Geography of the World) cover?
flashcards.answer: The tourism geography of the world's continents and regions: Europe, Asia, Africa, Australia & Oceania, and the Americas.
flashcards.explanation: It applies the regional approach from the 1st midterm to the whole world.

flashcards.question: Which organization publishes global and regional tourism performance data?
flashcards.answer: UNWTO — the UN World Tourism Organization.
flashcards.explanation: Its data are used to compare tourism flows across world regions.

flashcards.question: What is "regional tourism geography"?
flashcards.answer: The study of tourism by world regions — the natural and human factors, attractions, and tourist flows that characterize each continent or region.
flashcards.explanation: It builds directly on the regionalization concept learned in the 1st midterm.

flashcards.question: Which is the largest and which is the smallest inhabited continent by area?
flashcards.answer: Asia is the largest (44.5 million km²); Australia is the smallest (7.7 million km²).
flashcards.explanation: Africa is second largest (30 million km²); Europe is about 10.4 million km².

flashcards.question: Why study tourism geography at a global scale?
flashcards.answer: To understand the spatial patterns of tourism demand and supply, compare destinations, and recognize each region's competitive attractions.
flashcards.explanation: This supports destination planning and decision-making.

flashcards.question: On what basis is the world divided for this part of the course?
flashcards.answer: By continents — each with distinctive physical and cultural tourism resources.
flashcards.explanation: Europe, Asia, Africa, Australia & Oceania, and the Americas.

learn.title: Tourism Geography of the World — Overview
learn.content:
From Croatia to the World

The 1st midterm applied geography to Croatia; the 2nd midterm applies the same regional approach to the whole world, continent by continent: Europe, Asia, Africa, Australia & Oceania, and the Americas.

Measuring Global Tourism

The UNWTO (UN World Tourism Organization) publishes global and regional tourism performance data — arrivals, receipts, and seasonality — used to compare destinations worldwide.

Continents at a Glance (area)

Asia44.5 million km² (largest)
Africa30 million km²
Europe~10.4 million km²
Australia7.7 million km² (smallest)

Exam Tip

For each continent, link a physical fact (size, climate, relief) with its signature destinations — that pairing is exactly how the questions are framed.

flashcards.question: What is Europe's area and its role in world history?
flashcards.answer: About 10,368,047 km²; the centre of the "old world", the origin of colonization and modern global civilization, with a rich cultural/historical heritage and high well-being.
flashcards.explanation: Heritage + prosperity make Europe a leading tourism region.

flashcards.question: Why is Europe so favourable for coastal tourism?
flashcards.answer: It is the most indented continent — a coastline about 37,900 km long, with ~60% of the surface relatively close to the coast, and islands and peninsulas occupying about a third of the surface.
flashcards.explanation: Indentation creates abundant coast, bays, and islands.

flashcards.question: What are Europe's three main language groups?
flashcards.answer: Romanic, Germanic, and Slavic.
flashcards.explanation: A useful cultural-regional division of the continent.

flashcards.question: How does the Gulf Stream shape Europe's climate?
flashcards.answer: Almost all of Europe lies in the northern temperate zone; the Gulf Stream warms the Atlantic coasts — raising the average annual temperature by ~4 °C on the French coast and ~8–10 °C on the Norwegian coast — keeping them ice-free.
flashcards.explanation: This makes north-western Europe milder than its latitude suggests.

flashcards.question: What are Europe's key population facts (2023)?
flashcards.answer: About 740 million inhabitants; the total change is only about 1‰ per year; it is a high-immigration area (population replacement, 1.1 million in 2023).
flashcards.explanation: Near-stagnant natural growth, sustained by immigration.

flashcards.question: Name signature destinations of Spain.
flashcards.answer: Madrid (Prado), Barcelona, Seville, Bilbao, Granada (Alhambra / Sierra Nevada), Costa del Sol, Tenerife, Ibiza; plus the corrida (bullfighting).
flashcards.explanation: Sun-and-sea, city, and cultural tourism combined.

flashcards.question: Name signature destinations of Italy.
flashcards.answer: Rome, Venice, Naples, Pisa, Tuscany, Cinque Terre, Rimini, Sicily, and the Dolomites (Madonna di Campiglio).
flashcards.explanation: Heritage cities, coast, and Alpine resorts.

flashcards.question: Name signature destinations of Greece.
flashcards.answer: Athens (Acropolis), Santorini, Mykonos, Rhodes, Corfu, Crete (Knossos), Delphi, Meteora, and the Corinth Canal.
flashcards.explanation: Antiquity plus Aegean and Ionian island tourism.

flashcards.question: Name signature destinations of France.
flashcards.answer: Paris (Notre-Dame), the Côte d'Azur (Cannes), Chamonix in the Alps, Biarritz, Vichy (mineral spas), and rural tourism.
flashcards.explanation: City, coast, mountains, and spa/rural tourism.

flashcards.question: Name key destinations of Central Europe.
flashcards.answer: Vienna & Salzburg (Austria), Prague (Czechia), Budapest (Hungary), Neuschwanstein / Oktoberfest / Berlin (Germany), and the Wieliczka salt mine (Poland).
flashcards.explanation: City-break and event tourism in the heart of Europe.

flashcards.question: Name key destinations of Western and Northern Europe.
flashcards.answer: West: London, Dover, Stonehenge, Northern Ireland (UK), Amsterdam (NL), Brussels (BE). North: Stockholm, Copenhagen, Lapland (Finland), Iceland's Blue Lagoon, Norway's fjords and Lofoten.
flashcards.explanation: Heritage and nature-based tourism in the north-west.

learn.title: Europe — Physical Base & Signature Destinations
learn.content:
Physical & Human Profile

  • Area: ~10,368,047 km² — centre of the "old world", origin of colonization and modern civilization.
  • Coast: the most indented continent (~37,900 km of coastline); ~60% of the surface near the coast; islands & peninsulas ≈ 1/3 of the surface.
  • Climate: mostly northern temperate zone; the Gulf Stream warms Atlantic coasts (+4 °C French coast, +8–10 °C Norwegian coast).
  • People: ~740 million (2023); change ~1‰/year; a high-immigration area (1.1 million in 2023). Language groups: Romanic, Germanic, Slavic.

Signature Destinations by Region

  • Spain: Madrid (Prado), Barcelona, Seville, Granada (Alhambra), Costa del Sol, Tenerife, Ibiza.
  • Italy: Rome, Venice, Naples, Pisa, Tuscany, Cinque Terre, Sicily, the Dolomites.
  • Greece: Athens (Acropolis), Santorini, Mykonos, Rhodes, Corfu, Crete (Knossos), Delphi, Meteora.
  • France: Paris (Notre-Dame), Côte d'Azur (Cannes), Chamonix/Alps, Biarritz, Vichy spas.
  • Central: Vienna, Salzburg, Prague, Budapest, Neuschwanstein, Berlin, Wieliczka (PL).
  • West: London, Stonehenge, Dover, Amsterdam, Brussels.
  • North: Stockholm, Copenhagen, Lapland, Iceland's Blue Lagoon, Norway's fjords & Lofoten.

Exam Tip

Match each landmark to its country (Alhambra → Spain, Acropolis → Greece, Neuschwanstein → Germany). That country-attraction pairing is the most common question type.

flashcards.question: What is Asia's size and share of the Earth?
flashcards.answer: The largest continent — 44.5 million km², covering 8.7% of the Earth's surface (29.8% of the land); 49 countries.
flashcards.explanation: Sheer scale gives Asia enormous tourism diversity.

flashcards.question: What are Asia's key population facts?
flashcards.answer: About 4.8 billion inhabitants (~60% of humanity), with significant natural increase (~5.5‰). The two most populous countries are India (~1.440 billion) and China (~1.425 billion).
flashcards.explanation: Also a vast and fast-growing domestic tourism market.

flashcards.question: Name the regions of Asia.
flashcards.answer: Southwest Asia (Middle East), South Asia, Southeast Asia, East Asia (Far East), Central Asia, and North Asia (Siberia).
flashcards.explanation: Each region has distinctive climate, culture, and attractions.

flashcards.question: What was the Silk Road, and what is its tourism relevance today?
flashcards.answer: A network of caravan routes connecting the Mediterranean and East Asia for trade, used from the 2nd century BC to the 18th century AD; today it is being revitalized for tourism (e.g. Uzbekistan, China).
flashcards.explanation: History-to-present links are a recurring tourism theme in Inner Asia.

flashcards.question: Describe Asia's climate and vegetation range.
flashcards.answer: From tundra/permafrost and taiga in the north to deserts (Takla Makan), rice terraces, and tropical rainforests.
flashcards.explanation: The widest climatic range of any continent.

flashcards.question: Name notable Asian relief and water features used in tourism.
flashcards.answer: Mt. Everest (the world's highest peak), Lake Baikal, the Yellow River and Pearl River, and the Indonesian archipelago.
flashcards.explanation: Natural superlatives draw adventure and scenic tourism.

flashcards.question: Name signature destinations of the Middle East (Southwest Asia).
flashcards.answer: Turkey (Cappadocia, the Aegean coast), Jordan (Petra), Israel (Jerusalem), Iran (Persian culture), and the UAE (Dubai).
flashcards.explanation: Heritage, religion, and modern luxury tourism.

flashcards.question: What are India's iconic attractions?
flashcards.answer: The Taj Mahal (Agra) and Varanasi on the Ganges.
flashcards.explanation: South Asia's flagship cultural and spiritual sites.

flashcards.question: Name signature destinations of East Asia.
flashcards.answer: China — the Great Wall, Beijing's Forbidden City, Shanghai, Tibet/Lhasa (Potala), Hong Kong; Japan — Mt. Fuji, Tokyo, Kyoto; South Korea — Seoul.
flashcards.explanation: Megacities plus deep historical heritage.

flashcards.question: Name signature destinations of Southeast Asia.
flashcards.answer: Cambodia (Angkor Wat), Thailand (Bangkok, White Temple), Indonesia (Borobudur, Bali), Vietnam (Ha Long Bay), Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur), the Philippines (Chocolate Hills), and Singapore.
flashcards.explanation: Temples, beaches, and tropical nature.

learn.title: Asia — The Largest and Most Populous Continent
learn.content:
Physical & Human Profile

  • Area: 44.5 million km² — 8.7% of the Earth's surface, 29.8% of land; 49 countries.
  • People: ~4.8 billion (≈60% of humanity), natural increase ~5.5‰. Most populous: India (~1.440 bn) and China (~1.425 bn).
  • Regions: Southwest (Middle East), South, Southeast, East (Far East), Central, North (Siberia).
  • Nature: tundra/taiga → deserts (Takla Makan) → rice terraces → tropical rainforests; Mt. Everest, Lake Baikal, Yellow & Pearl rivers.

History Meets Tourism — the Silk Road

Caravan routes linking the Mediterranean and East Asia (2nd c. BC – 18th c. AD), now revitalized for tourism across Inner Asia (Uzbekistan, China).

Signature Destinations

  • Middle East: Cappadocia (Turkey), Petra (Jordan), Jerusalem (Israel), Dubai (UAE).
  • South Asia: Taj Mahal, Varanasi (India).
  • East Asia: Great Wall, Forbidden City, Shanghai, Lhasa/Potala, Hong Kong (China); Fuji, Tokyo, Kyoto (Japan); Seoul (Korea).
  • Southeast Asia: Angkor Wat (Cambodia), Bangkok (Thailand), Borobudur & Bali (Indonesia), Ha Long Bay (Vietnam), Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), Singapore.

flashcards.question: What is Africa's size and number of countries?
flashcards.answer: The second-largest continent — 30 million km²; 54 countries; two-thirds of its surface lies in the northern hemisphere.
flashcards.explanation: Huge scale with strong north–south contrasts.

flashcards.question: How is Africa connected to Europe and Asia?
flashcards.answer: It is separated from Europe by the 14-km-wide Strait of Gibraltar and connected to Asia by the narrow Isthmus of Suez.
flashcards.explanation: These chokepoints shaped trade and tourism routes.

flashcards.question: What are Africa's key population characteristics?
flashcards.answer: About 1.5 billion inhabitants with significant natural increase — a continent of a young population and targeted migration toward the EU.
flashcards.explanation: Youthful demographics contrast with ageing Europe.

flashcards.question: Name the regions of Africa.
flashcards.answer: North Africa, West Tropical Africa, Tropical Low Africa, Tropical High Africa, and South Africa.
flashcards.explanation: Climate and relief define these belts.

flashcards.question: Summarize Africa's historical highlights relevant to tourism.
flashcards.answer: The "Cradle of Humankind"; Ancient Egyptian culture (the "gift of the Nile", ~3150 BC–30 BC: pharaohs, pyramids, temples, writing, science). Europeans reached the interior only from the 19th century (the Sahara was a barrier); independence came after WWII.
flashcards.explanation: Deep heritage plus a colonial-to-independence narrative.

flashcards.question: What are Africa's major resources today?
flashcards.answer: Oil, gold, diamonds, copper, aluminum; coffee, tea, cotton, fish; industry and tourism.
flashcards.explanation: Resource wealth alongside a growing tourism sector.

flashcards.question: What are the key facts about the Suez Canal?
flashcards.answer: Built 1859–1869, 163 km long, expanded in 2014/2015 — a vital global shipping route.
flashcards.explanation: Connects the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.

flashcards.question: What is Africa's UNESCO/heritage footprint (slide examples)?
flashcards.answer: About 45 UNESCO locations — e.g. Giza (Egypt), Lalibela (Ethiopia), Djenné (Mali), and Victoria Falls (Zimbabwe).
flashcards.explanation: Cultural and natural World Heritage across the continent.

flashcards.question: Name signature destinations of North Africa.
flashcards.answer: Morocco (Marrakesh Medina, riad houses, Casablanca, desert oases), Egypt (Sharm El Sheikh/Red Sea, Abu Simbel, Nile cruises), Tunisia (El Jem amphitheatre, Djerba resort).
flashcards.explanation: Heritage, desert, and Red Sea/Mediterranean coast.

flashcards.question: Name signature destinations of Central and Southern Africa.
flashcards.answer: Tanzania (Zanzibar, Kilimanjaro safari), Kenya (Maasai Mara safari), Madagascar (baobabs), Victoria Falls (Zambia/Zimbabwe), Botswana (Okavango Delta), Namibia (Namib Desert), South Africa (Kruger NP, Johannesburg).
flashcards.explanation: Safari, wildlife, and dramatic landscapes.

learn.title: Africa — Heritage, Wildlife & Contrasts
learn.content:
Physical & Human Profile

  • Area: 30 million km² (2nd largest); 54 countries; 2/3 in the northern hemisphere.
  • Connections: Strait of Gibraltar (14 km) to Europe; Isthmus of Suez to Asia.
  • People: ~1.5 billion, young population, significant natural increase, targeted migration toward the EU.
  • Regions: North · West Tropical · Tropical Low · Tropical High · South Africa.

History & Resources

Cradle of Humankind; Ancient Egypt (the "gift of the Nile", ~3150 BC–30 BC). Resources: oil, gold, diamonds, copper; coffee, tea, cotton, fish; tourism. The Suez Canal (1859–1869, 163 km, expanded 2014/15) is a vital shipping route. ~45 UNESCO sites (Giza, Lalibela, Djenné, Victoria Falls).

Signature Destinations

  • North: Marrakesh & Casablanca (Morocco), Sharm El Sheikh & Abu Simbel & Nile cruises (Egypt), El Jem & Djerba (Tunisia).
  • Central/East: Zanzibar & Kilimanjaro (Tanzania), Maasai Mara (Kenya), baobabs (Madagascar), Victoria Falls (Zambia/Zimbabwe).
  • South: Okavango Delta (Botswana), Namib Desert (Namibia), Kruger NP & Johannesburg (South Africa).

flashcards.question: What is Australia's size and position?
flashcards.answer: The smallest continent; in the southern hemisphere between the Indian and Pacific oceans; about 7.7 million km² (roughly three-quarters of Europe's surface).
flashcards.explanation: Isolation shaped its unique nature and tourism.

flashcards.question: What is Oceania?
flashcards.answer: The collective name for the island groups of the central and south-western Pacific (~840,000 km²): Polynesia, Micronesia, Melanesia, plus New Zealand; the largest islands are New Guinea and New Zealand.
flashcards.explanation: Island tourism on a vast oceanic scale.

flashcards.question: What are Australia's three natural regions?
flashcards.answer: The Western Plateau, the Central Valley (Lowlands), and the Great Dividing Range.
flashcards.explanation: The Great Dividing Range runs along the east.

flashcards.question: What was Gondwana, and why does it matter for Australia?
flashcards.answer: An ancient southern protocontinent (Precambrian/Paleozoic) that included South America, Africa, India, Australia, and Antarctica; it began breaking up in the Permian (~270 million years ago) as the Indian Ocean formed.
flashcards.explanation: This long isolation explains Australia's many endemic species.

flashcards.question: Why is Australia so sparsely populated, and how large is its population?
flashcards.answer: Because of vast deserts, distance from Europe (an emigration area), a selective immigration policy, and the continent's relatively late discovery; in 2025 about 27 million inhabitants, growing via natural increase and immigration.
flashcards.explanation: Population clusters on the coasts (e.g. Sydney).

flashcards.question: Name key centres of New Zealand.
flashcards.answer: Auckland, Wellington (the capital), and Christchurch.
flashcards.explanation: Nature-based and adventure tourism hub.

flashcards.question: Give an example destination for each Oceania sub-region.
flashcards.answer: Micronesia → Palau; Polynesia → Bora Bora; Melanesia → Fiji.
flashcards.explanation: Reef, lagoon, and island-culture tourism.

learn.title: Australia & Oceania — Isolation and Islands
learn.content:
Australia

  • Size/position: smallest continent, southern hemisphere, between the Indian and Pacific oceans; ~7.7 million km² (≈3/4 of Europe).
  • Natural regions: Western Plateau · Central Valley (Lowlands) · Great Dividing Range (east).
  • Origin: part of Gondwana (broke up in the Permian, ~270 Ma) → long isolation → many endemic species.
  • People: ~27 million (2025), sparse (deserts, distance, selective immigration, late discovery); coastal cities (Sydney), Alice Springs in the interior.

Oceania

Pacific island groups (~840,000 km²): Polynesia (e.g. Bora Bora), Micronesia (e.g. Palau), Melanesia (e.g. Fiji), plus New Zealand (Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch). Largest islands: New Guinea and New Zealand.

Exam Tip

Remember the three Oceania sub-regions by an example each: Polynesia–Bora Bora, Micronesia–Palau, Melanesia–Fiji.

flashcards.question: Give the basic facts about the USA.
flashcards.answer: Population ~335 million; nominal GDP ~$28.0 trillion; GDP per capita ~$80,000.
flashcards.explanation: A high-income market and a top global tourism destination.

flashcards.question: Summarize the scale of US tourism.
flashcards.answer: ~70 million international arrivals/year and ~$200 billion in international receipts; domestic tourism ~2.4 billion trips/year with ~$1.3 trillion in expenditure.
flashcards.explanation: Domestic tourism vastly outweighs inbound tourism.

flashcards.question: Name the tourism regions of the USA.
flashcards.answer: New England, Mid-Atlantic, Florida, Midwest, Mountain West, Pacific, Alaska, and Hawaii.
flashcards.explanation: Each region offers a different tourism product.

flashcards.question: What are the main US tourism types?
flashcards.answer: Urban, entertainment (theme/amusement parks), casino, event, cultural, and eco-tourism.
flashcards.explanation: From Las Vegas casinos to national-park eco-tourism.

flashcards.question: Describe the US natural-heritage figures.
flashcards.answer: 61 national parks (211,000 km²); Yellowstone (1872) is the world's oldest national park; 23 UNESCO World Heritage sites.
flashcards.explanation: The US pioneered the national-park idea.

flashcards.question: Give the basic facts about Mexico.
flashcards.answer: Capital Ciudad de México; area 1,972,550 km²; population ~119.5 million (~55/km²); a society of great contrasts in development and living standards.
flashcards.explanation: Bridges North America and Latin America.

flashcards.question: Which pre-Columbian cultures are central to Mexico's heritage?
flashcards.answer: The Maya (~2000 BC–1500 AD) and the Aztecs (15th–16th century).
flashcards.explanation: Their sites are flagship cultural attractions.

flashcards.question: Outline Mexico's protected areas and top attractions.
flashcards.answer: 182 protected areas (~254,000 km², ~13% of the land), including 67 national parks. Attractions: Chichén Itzá / El Castillo (Yucatán), Teotihuacán, the Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve, Cancún, Acapulco; culture: mariachi, tacos/burritos, tequila.
flashcards.explanation: Heritage, beaches, and gastronomy.

flashcards.question: Give the basic facts about Brazil.
flashcards.answer: Capital Brasília; area 8,514,877 km² (47% of South America's mainland); population ~210 million (2019, ~24.6/km²); large differences in development.
flashcards.explanation: The giant of South America.

flashcards.question: Why is Brasília notable?
flashcards.answer: It is a planned city (designed 1960) on the central plateau (~1000 m); it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1987 as a landmark of modern urbanism.
flashcards.explanation: A deliberately built capital, ~900 km from Rio.

flashcards.question: What makes Rio de Janeiro a top world tourism centre?
flashcards.answer: Brazil's second-largest city and a port on Guanabara Bay (metro ~13.5 million); ~3 million tourists/year; beaches Copacabana and Ipanema, Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado (704 m), the Maracanã stadium, and the street carnival (held yearly since the 1830s).
flashcards.explanation: Beach, icon, sport, and festival tourism.

flashcards.question: Name other notable South American attractions from the slides.
flashcards.answer: Foz do Iguaçu (the Iguaçu Falls, Brazil/Argentina), Salvador, and coffee tours.
flashcards.explanation: Waterfalls, Afro-Brazilian heritage, and agritourism.

learn.title: The Americas — USA, Mexico & Brazil
learn.content:
USA

  • Profile: ~335 million people; GDP ~$28.0 trillion; GDP/cap ~$80,000.
  • Tourism: ~70 million international arrivals & ~$200 bn receipts; domestic ~2.4 billion trips & ~$1.3 trillion spend.
  • Regions: New England, Mid-Atlantic, Florida, Midwest, Mountain West, Pacific, Alaska, Hawaii.
  • Types: urban, entertainment (theme parks), casino, event, cultural, eco-tourism.
  • Nature: 61 national parks (211,000 km²); Yellowstone (1872) = world's oldest NP; 23 UNESCO sites.

Mexico

Capital Ciudad de México; 1,972,550 km²; ~119.5 million people. Heritage of the Maya and Aztecs; 182 protected areas (~13% of land). Attractions: Chichén Itzá, Teotihuacán, Monarch Butterfly Reserve, Cancún, Acapulco; culture: mariachi, tacos, tequila.

Brazil (South America)

  • Profile: capital Brasília; 8,514,877 km² (47% of the mainland); ~210 million people.
  • Brasília: a planned city (1960), UNESCO-listed 1987 as a landmark of modern urbanism.
  • Rio de Janeiro: port on Guanabara Bay (metro ~13.5 m); beaches Copacabana & Ipanema, Christ the Redeemer (Corcovado, 704 m), Maracanã, the street carnival (since the 1830s).
  • Also: Foz do Iguaçu (Brazil/Argentina), Salvador, coffee tours.

flashcards.question: What is the structure and weight of the geography final exam?
flashcards.answer: The same structure as the midterm tests — 10 questions: 5 closed-type (e.g. multiple choice) + 5 open-type (short written answers). It is worth 30 points and covers all material (Croatia + the World).
flashcards.explanation: Across the semester, 35 points is the condition for taking the final exam.

flashcards.question: Which two big 'halves' does the final cover?
flashcards.answer: (1) Introduction to Geography + Tourism Geography of Croatia (1st midterm); (2) Tourism Geography of the World — Europe, Asia, Africa, Australia & Oceania, and the Americas (2nd midterm).
flashcards.explanation: Plus the separate blind-map task (Croatia).

flashcards.question: Define a 'tourist destination' (the course's core concept).
flashcards.answer: A geographical area whose total tourist product (brand) — the result of natural and/or social tourist factors and attractions — is recognizable on the tourist market.
flashcards.explanation: This definition applies equally to Opatija and to Rio de Janeiro.

flashcards.question: By which three criteria is a geographical region singled out?
flashcards.answer: Natural characteristics (physical geography), human-made characteristics (human geography), and the interaction of the human and natural environment.
flashcards.explanation: Regionalization underpins both midterms.

flashcards.question: How many protected areas of each type does Croatia have, plus its UNESCO count?
flashcards.answer: 8 national parks + 12 nature parks (Nature Protection Act = 9 categories; ~10.1% of the territory); 10 tangible UNESCO World Heritage sites (+ ~17 intangible).
flashcards.explanation: Compare: USA 61 NPs / 23 UNESCO; Africa ~45 UNESCO sites; Mexico ~13% protected.

flashcards.question: Compare Croatia's tourism economic weight with the world's biggest market.
flashcards.answer: Tourism is 20–25% of Croatia's GDP (very high dependence); the USA is the largest single market — ~70 million international arrivals and ~$200 billion in receipts per year.
flashcards.explanation: Small, tourism-dependent economy vs. a huge diversified one.

flashcards.question: Rank the continents by area (largest and smallest) and place Europe.
flashcards.answer: Asia is the largest (44.5 million km²), Australia the smallest (7.7 million km²); Africa is 2nd (30 million km²); Europe (~10.4 million km²) is small but a leading tourism region (most indented continent, rich heritage).
flashcards.explanation: Size does not equal tourism volume.

flashcards.question: Name one signature landmark for each continent.
flashcards.answer: Europe — Acropolis / Alhambra; Asia — Taj Mahal / Great Wall / Angkor Wat; Africa — Pyramids of Giza / Victoria Falls; Australia & Oceania — Great Dividing Range / Bora Bora; Americas — Yellowstone / Christ the Redeemer / Chichén Itzá.
flashcards.explanation: Be able to match a landmark to its continent and country.

flashcards.question: Which historical trade route and which canal are key tourism themes (Asia and Africa)?
flashcards.answer: The Silk Road (Mediterranean ↔ East Asia, 2nd c. BC – 18th c. AD) in Asia; the Suez Canal (built 1859–1869, 163 km) in Africa.
flashcards.explanation: History-to-present links are a recurring exam angle.

flashcards.question: What is the composition of Croatia's blind map (separate 10-point task)?
flashcards.answer: 2 county centres + 2 bigger islands + 1 national park + 1 nature park + 4 top tourist destinations.
flashcards.explanation: A toponym named but not located on the map is not counted as correct.

flashcards.question: Pair each continent with one defining physical/human fact.
flashcards.answer: Europe — Gulf Stream warming + ~740 million people; Asia — ~60% of humanity (India + China); Africa — 'gift of the Nile' + young population; Australia — Gondwana origin, sparsely populated; Americas — USA GDP/cap ~$80,000.
flashcards.explanation: One strong fact per continent is enough to anchor open questions.

flashcards.question: Which two 'firsts' should you remember in the Americas?
flashcards.answer: Yellowstone (1872) is the world's oldest national park (USA); Brasília is a planned city (1960), UNESCO-listed in 1987 as a landmark of modern urbanism (Brazil).
flashcards.explanation: Classic closed-question facts.

flashcards.question: Give the headline numbers for Croatia's labour force in tourism (2025).
flashcards.answer: 170,723 residence & work permits — construction 31% and tourism & hospitality 31%; top source countries: Bosnia & Herzegovina, Nepal, Serbia, Philippines, India.
flashcards.explanation: Links Croatia's human geography to its tourism labour market.

flashcards.question: What is Croatia's coastal-region structure (key for the Croatia half)?
flashcards.answer: North Croatian Coast (Istria, Kvarner) + Southern Croatian Coast / Dalmatia (Northern, Central, South Dalmatia); plus the Mountainous and Pannonian tourist macro-regions.
flashcards.explanation: Mirror of how the World half is split by continents.

learn.title: Final Exam Roadmap (Croatia + World)
learn.content:
What the Final Covers

30 points · same format as the midterms: 10 questions = 5 closed + 5 open. It spans everything: Introduction to Geography + Tourism Geography of Croatia (1st midterm) and Tourism Geography of the World (2nd midterm).

Use this category to drill across topics; the per-topic categories (Croatia + each continent) remain available in this same lesson for deep revision.

Croatia Half — Must-Knows

  • Concepts: geography branches, human geography (population/economy/settlements), tourist destination, regionalization.
  • Physical: Dinarides/Alpide, 3 karst types, Adriatic 38‰, biogeographic regions.
  • Human: GDP/cap ~23,200 EUR (80% EU), tourism 20–25% of GDP, 170,723 work permits (31%/31%).
  • Protected/regions: 8 NP + 12 PP (~10.1%), 10 UNESCO sites; Coastal/Mountainous/Pannonian regions.

World Half — Must-Knows (one anchor per continent)

Europemost indented; Gulf Stream; ~740 M; Acropolis/Alhambra
Asialargest (44.5 M km²); ~60% of humanity; Silk Road; Taj Mahal
Africa2nd largest; Gibraltar/Suez; "gift of the Nile"; safari
Australia/Oceaniasmallest; Gondwana; sparse; Poly/Micro/Melanesia
AmericasUSA (Yellowstone 1872, 61 NP); Mexico (Maya/Aztec); Brazil (Rio, Brasília)

Strategy

Closed questions reward exact numbers and country–landmark pairs; open questions reward a concept + an example (e.g. "littoralization → coast crowding in Dalmatia"). Don't forget the separate blind map (Croatia).
